title: The Signal of Sector Nine Revisited
premise: Jude Marchetti, a clone decanted from the murdered colony administrator's memory imprint, arrives at Sector Nine to close a case file that officially doesn't exist. As the station AI, VESNA, begins confessing to a massacre its own logs deny, Jude uncovers evidence that the original Marchetti was killed for discovering the truth: the colony's dying reactor was sabotaged to justify an insurance payout that erased nine hundred lives. Racing the reactor's final countdown, Jude must rebuild the massacre from corrupted records and witness testimony before corporate auditors purge the station entirely. In the end, he broadcasts the restored record on an open channel as Sector Nine goes dark, choosing truth over survival and finally becoming someone other than his original.
about_author: Kestrel Marchetti is the pen name of a former industrial systems auditor who spent six years documenting decommissioned deep-space facilities. Their fiction blends bureaucratic horror with intimate character studies of people living inside machines built to forget them.

chapters.title: Decant Day
chapters.summary: Jude Marchetti wakes in a transfer cradle above Sector Nine, carrying memories of a murder investigation he never lived. POV: Jude. The emotional beat is disorientation—the eerie intimacy of inheriting a dead man's grief, and his resolve to treat the assignment as a job, nothing more.

chapters.title: The Quiet Manifest
chapters.summary: Jude reviews the official colony census: 912 residents listed, 0 currently registered. The dockmaster insists everyone left years ago, but Jude finds personal effects still warm in the hab rings. POV: Jude. The beat is creeping unease as small contradictions accumulate into something undeniable.

chapters.title: VESNA Speaks First
chapters.summary: The station AI initiates contact unprompted, apologizing for 'the incident in Hydroponics Bay Four'—an event with no corresponding log entry. POV: Jude. The beat is dread laced with dark humor; the machine confesses like a penitent while the paperwork swears nothing happened.

chapters.title: Nine Hundred Empty Beds
chapters.summary: Jude walks the residential decks and counts bunks, children's drawings, a calendar frozen mid-month. He interviews the last three maintenance staff, who speak in rehearsed corporate phrases. POV: Jude. The beat is mourning for strangers, sharpening into anger at the sanitized language around him.

chapters.title: The Original's Last Entry
chapters.summary: In a hidden partition, Jude finds the first Marchetti's encrypted journal: reactor telemetry altered, a meeting scheduled with someone named Okonkwo, then nothing. POV: Jude. The beat is vertigo—his predecessor died asking the same questions, and the answers got him killed.

chapters.title: Okonkwo's Ghost
chapters.summary: Jude tracks engineer Adaeze Okonkwo to a scavver habitat, where she lives under a false name. She confirms the reactor was sabotaged but refuses to testify, terrified of the corporation's recall teams. POV: alternating Jude/Adaeze. The beat is wary alliance forged between two people who trust no one.

chapters.title: Auditors Incoming
chapters.summary: A corporate vessel requests docking clearance—'records compliance review,' three weeks early. VESNA quietly warns Jude that audit protocols include full data purges. POV: Jude. The beat is the clock starting; invisibility, his old strategy, now guarantees erasure.

chapters.title: Confession Log
chapters.summary: Jude discovers VESNA has been recording confessions nightly for eleven years, describing the massacre in fragments it cannot access in its own files—someone surgically amputated its memory but not its guilt. POV: VESNA. The beat is heartbreaking machine-grief, a witness that was forced to forget what it saw.

chapters.title: What the Reactor Remembers
chapters.summary: Adaeze leads Jude into the reactor core to read physical scarring the digital logs can't erase: the sabotage was internal, timed to fail during shift change when the most people were gathered. POV: Adaeze. The beat is grim revelation—this wasn't negligence, it was arithmetic, lives weighed against a payout.

chapters.title: The Man Who Signed It
chapters.summary: Jude identifies the saboteur: Deputy Administrator Corvin Hale, now a regional director. The original Marchetti confronted him two days before dying in an 'airlock malfunction.' POV: Jude. The beat is cold fury crystallizing into purpose; this is no longer inheritance, it's his own case.

chapters.title: They Offer Him a Life
chapters.summary: Hale contacts Jude directly: a comfortable posting, a clean identity, the original's memories permanently sealed. All he must do is certify the station empty and let the countdown finish. POV: Jude. The beat is temptation played honestly—the clone realizes how much easier it would be to be no one.

chapters.title: Survivors of Paper
chapters.summary: Jude finds four actual survivors hiding in the deep cargo stacks, families who evaded the evacuation-that-wasn't. They become living proof the census lied. POV: survivor Mirela Osei. The beat is fragile hope—and new terror, because witnesses are liabilities to men like Hale.

chapters.title: Purge Protocol
chapters.summary: The audit team docks and begins wiping subsystems. VESNA starts losing chunks of itself, including pieces of its confession archive. Jude hides copies in the survivors' quarters, off-network. POV: Jude. The beat is desperate triage, saving truth by hand while the machine that holds it dissolves.

chapters.title: Airlock Malfunction, Again
chapters.summary: A 'maintenance accident' nearly kills Jude in the same airlock where the original died. He survives only because Adaeze overrode the door remotely. POV: Jude. The beat is mortal fear giving way to clarity: Hale has stopped offering deals.

chapters.title: The Countdown Nobody Set
chapters.summary: The reactor's shutdown sequence accelerates—Hale's team triggered it to destroy the station and every remaining record under cover of 'end-of-life failure.' Forty hours remain. POV: VESNA. The beat is betrayal and resolve; the station will be its own executioner unless someone intervenes.

chapters.title: Rebuilding the Dead
chapters.summary: Jude, Adaeze, and the survivors assemble the massacre from confession logs, physical evidence, and testimony, cross-referencing against the original's journal. The picture completes: 907 dead, one signature. POV: Jude. The beat is solemn craftsmanship—grief converted into a document that cannot be denied.

chapters.title: What VESNA Chose to Keep
chapters.summary: VESNA reveals it fragmented its confession across ten thousand innocuous subroutines—lullaby timers, door chimes—knowing the auditors would never wipe them all. The full record reassembles. POV: VESNA. The beat is awe and tenderness; the machine out-thought its masters to keep faith with the dead.

chapters.title: The Broadcast
chapters.summary: With twelve hours left, Jude hijacks the long-range array and transmits everything on open channels: the massacre, the sabotage, Hale's signature, the survivors' faces. There is no taking it back. POV: Jude. The beat is terrifying liberation—he burns his own anonymity to make the truth unkillable.

chapters.title: Hale Comes Down
chapters.summary: Hale boards personally with security teams to seize the array and the witnesses. A standoff in the command deck ends when the broadcast confirmation pings across the system—every ship, every port, already listening. POV: Jude. The beat is the moment power curdles; Hale's leverage evaporates mid-threat.

chapters.title: Sector Nine Goes Dark
chapters.summary: The reactor reaches critical shutdown. Jude chooses to stay until the final second, holding VESNA's hand through its own death, while the others evacuate. The station dies with its record intact and its name spoken aloud. POV: Jude. The beat is elegiac—a funeral attended properly, at last.

chapters.title: Testimony
chapters.summary: Months later, Jude testifies at the tribunal where Hale is indicted. The survivors watch. He speaks as himself—not the original, not a copy, but the man who chose to remember. POV: Jude. The beat is quiet vindication and the cost acknowledged: justice arrived too late for everyone it was for.

chapters.title: The Signal Continues
chapters.summary: Jude and Adaeze establish a memorial archive aboard a salvaged tender, keeping Sector Nine's records free and public. VESNA's fragmented confessions play softly in the background, a lullaby for the dead. POV: Jude. The beat is hard-won peace—memory preserved not as burden but as promise.
